action.yml:
name: Install Whitaker
description: Install the Whitaker Dylint suite with a cached installer

inputs:
  cargo-home:
    description: Cargo home that stores the cached whitaker-installer binary
    required: false
    default: ~/.cargo
  installer-version:
    description: >-
      Version of whitaker-installer to install. Defaults to the version this
      action pins, and must be 0.2.9 or later: that is the first release with
      --no-source-fallback, which the action always passes.
    required: false
    default: "0.2.9"
  installer-sha256:
    description: >-
      SHA-256 digest of the whitaker-installer release archive for this
      runner. The action's pinned digest manifest takes precedence; supply
      this only for an asset the manifest does not pin. A value that
      disagrees with a pinned digest is rejected.
    required: false
    default: ""
  suite-version:
    description: >-
      Refused. Whitaker's lint suite is a rolling release that every consumer
      takes from the default branch tip, and a pin would force a source
      build. The input stays declared only so that setting it fails the step:
      GitHub drops an undeclared input with a warning, which would let a pin
      look honoured while doing nothing.
    required: false
    default: ""
  cache-provider:
    description: >-
      Cache owner for the installer binary. Use "github" for the action's
      built-in cache or "external" when the caller mounts the Cargo home.
    required: false
    default: "github"
  ci-mode:
    description: >-
      Check the published lint assets before running the installer, retrying
      a short absence while the rolling release republishes. A source build is
      refused either way: the installer always receives --no-source-fallback,
      and a run whose output still reports one fails. Set it off only where
      the rolling release cannot be reached, such as a local reproduction.
    required: false
    default: "true"
  cranelift:
    description: >-
      Also install the rustc-codegen-cranelift component for the lint suite's
      toolchain, for a repository whose builds select the Cranelift backend.
      The installer adds the component through rustup; nothing is compiled.
    required: false
    default: "false"
  github-token:
    description: >-
      Token used only to read the public rolling release without meeting the
      unauthenticated rate limit. It is never sent anywhere else.
    required: false
    default: ${{ github.token }}

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Validate Whitaker inputs
      id: validate-inputs
      shell: bash
      env:
        CACHE_PROVIDER_INPUT: ${{ inputs.cache-provider }}
        CARGO_HOME_INPUT: ${{ inputs.cargo-home }}
        CI_MODE_INPUT: ${{ inputs.ci-mode }}
        CRANELIFT_INPUT: ${{ inputs.cranelift }}
        INSTALLER_SHA256_INPUT: ${{ inputs.installer-sha256 }}
        INSTALLER_VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.installer-version }}
        SUITE_VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.suite-version }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        input_error() {
          echo "::error title=Invalid Whitaker input::$1" >&2
          exit 1
        }
        if [[ -z "${RUNNER_TEMP:-}" ]]; then
          input_error "RUNNER_TEMP must name a writable staging directory"
        fi
        if [[ "$CARGO_HOME_INPUT" == *$'\r'* || "$CARGO_HOME_INPUT" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
          input_error "cargo-home must not contain a carriage return or newline"
        fi
        if [[ "$INSTALLER_VERSION_INPUT" == *$'\r'* || "$INSTALLER_VERSION_INPUT" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
          input_error "installer-version must not contain a carriage return or newline"
        fi
        case "$CACHE_PROVIDER_INPUT" in
          github|external) ;;
          *) input_error "cache-provider must be github or external" ;;
        esac
        case "$CRANELIFT_INPUT" in
          true|false) ;;
          *) input_error "cranelift must be true or false" ;;
        esac
        case "$CI_MODE_INPUT" in
          true|false) ;;
          *) input_error "ci-mode must be true or false" ;;
        esac
        # The lint suite is a rolling release: every consumer takes it from the
        # Whitaker default branch tip, and prebuilt lint libraries exist only
        # for that tip, so a pin would also force a source build. Rejected
        # rather than ignored, so a lane cannot believe it is pinned.
        if [[ -n "$SUITE_VERSION_INPUT" ]]; then
          input_error "suite-version is refused: the Whitaker lint suite is a rolling release and is never pinned"
        fi
        if (( ${#CARGO_HOME_INPUT} > 240 )); then
          input_error "cargo-home must be at most 240 characters"
        fi
        if (( ${#INSTALLER_VERSION_INPUT} > 128 )); then
          input_error "installer-version must be at most 128 characters"
        fi
        if [[ ! "$INSTALLER_VERSION_INPUT" =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)){0,2}$ ]]; then
          input_error "installer-version must be one to three numeric components without leading zeros"
        fi
        # 0.2.9 is the first installer with --no-source-fallback, which the run
        # step always passes. An older installer rejects the flag, so the floor
        # is enforced here, where the cause is legible, rather than as an
        # unknown-argument failure after the download.
        IFS=. read -r version_major version_minor version_patch <<< "$INSTALLER_VERSION_INPUT"
        version_minor="${version_minor:-0}"
        version_patch="${version_patch:-0}"
        if (( version_major == 0 && (version_minor < 2 || (version_minor == 2 && version_patch < 9)) )); then
          input_error "installer-version ${INSTALLER_VERSION_INPUT} is below the 0.2.9 floor, the first release with --no-source-fallback"
        fi
        installer_sha256=
        if [[ -n "$INSTALLER_SHA256_INPUT" ]]; then
          if [[ ! "$INSTALLER_SHA256_INPUT" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$ ]]; then
            input_error "installer-sha256 must be 64 hexadecimal characters"
          fi
          installer_sha256="$(printf '%s' "$INSTALLER_SHA256_INPUT" | tr 'A-F' 'a-f')"
        fi
        if [[ "$CARGO_HOME_INPUT" == "~" || "$CARGO_HOME_INPUT" == "~/"* ]]; then
          cargo_home="${HOME}${CARGO_HOME_INPUT:1}"
        elif [[ "$CARGO_HOME_INPUT" == /* ]]; then
          cargo_home="$CARGO_HOME_INPUT"
        else
          input_error "cargo-home must be an absolute path or start with ~/"
        fi
        if [[ "/${cargo_home}/" == *"/../"* ]]; then
          input_error "cargo-home must not contain parent-directory components"
        fi
        path_separator=:
        if [[ "${RUNNER_OS:-}" == Windows ]]; then
          path_separator=';'
        fi
        if [[ "$cargo_home" == *"$path_separator"* ]]; then
          input_error "cargo-home must not contain the runner PATH separator"
        fi
        mkdir -p -- "$cargo_home"
        cargo_home="$(cd -- "$cargo_home" && pwd -P)"
        if [[ "$cargo_home" == *"$path_separator"* ]]; then
          input_error "cargo-home must not contain the runner PATH separator"
        fi
        printf 'cargo-home=%s\n' "$cargo_home" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        installer_suffix=
        if [[ "${RUNNER_OS:-}" == Windows ]]; then
          installer_suffix=.exe
        fi
        printf 'installer-path=%s\n' "${cargo_home}/bin/whitaker-installer${installer_suffix}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        printf 'installer-version-path=%s\n' "${cargo_home}/bin/.whitaker-installer-version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        printf 'installer-version=%s\n' "$INSTALLER_VERSION_INPUT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        printf 'installer-sha256=%s\n' "$installer_sha256" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    - name: Cache Whitaker installer
      id: cache-whitaker-installer
      if: ${{ inputs.cache-provider == 'github' }}
      uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
      with:
        path: |
          ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-path }}
          ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version-path }}
          ~/.local/share/whitaker
        key: >-
          whitaker-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version }}-${{ hashFiles('dylint.toml') }}-${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.cargo-home }}

    - name: Report Whitaker installer cache
      shell: bash
      env:
        WHITAKER_CACHE_PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.cache-provider }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_CACHE_HIT: ${{ steps.cache-whitaker-installer.outputs.cache-hit }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        emit_metric() {
          if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
        }
        cache_state=disabled
        if [[ "$WHITAKER_CACHE_PROVIDER" == github && "$WHITAKER_INSTALLER_CACHE_HIT" == true ]]; then
          cache_state=hit
        elif [[ "$WHITAKER_CACHE_PROVIDER" == github ]]; then
          cache_state=miss
        fi
        echo "::notice title=Whitaker installer cache::provider=${WHITAKER_CACHE_PROVIDER} state=${cache_state} version=${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}"
        emit_metric "whitaker-installer.cache=${cache_state}"

    - name: Resolve Whitaker release
      id: resolve-release
      shell: bash
      env:
        RUNNER_ARCHITECTURE: ${{ runner.arch }}
        RUNNER_OPERATING_SYSTEM: ${{ runner.os }}
        WHITAKER_DIGEST_MANIFEST: ${{ github.action_path }}/installer-digests.sha256
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_PATH: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-path }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_SHA256: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-sha256 }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION_PATH: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version-path }}
        WHITAKER_RESOLVE_SCRIPT: ${{ github.action_path }}/scripts/resolve-release.sh
        WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/whitaker-installer-release
      run: |
        # Thin command adapter. The resolution itself lives in
        # scripts/resolve-release.sh, which only prints; this step captures
        # that record and writes it to the step output, the one mechanism for
        # carrying a value across a composite step boundary. The publication
        # step turns the record into outputs, metrics, notices, and the job's
        # fate.
        set -Eeuo pipefail
        emit_metric() {
          if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
        }
        # Reports only an unexpected internal failure, such as awk dying or the
        # resolve script being unreadable. An expected resolution failure is a
        # record printed by the script.
        trap 'status=$?; echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::resolution failed with exit-code=${status} version=${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}" >&2; emit_metric "whitaker-installer.failure=resolve"; exit "${status}"' ERR
        # RUNNER_TEMP is a native path, so under Git Bash the staging
        # directory arrives as D:\a\_temp/... . GNU tar reads a colon in an
        # archive path as rmt's host:path syntax and tries to resolve the
        # drive letter as a hostname. Normalize here, where the path is first
        # produced, so download, verify, extract, and install all receive the
        # POSIX form rather than each having to cope.
        if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR="$(cygpath -u "$WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR")"
          export WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR
        fi
        resolution="$(bash "$WHITAKER_RESOLVE_SCRIPT")"
        {
          printf 'resolution<<WHITAKER_RESOLUTION_EOF\n'
          printf '%s\n' "$resolution"
          printf 'WHITAKER_RESOLUTION_EOF\n'
        } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    - name: Publish Whitaker resolution
      id: publish-resolution
      shell: bash
      env:
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version }}
        WHITAKER_RESOLUTION: ${{ steps.resolve-release.outputs.resolution }}
      run: |
        # Publication. Every externally visible effect of resolution lives
        # here: the step outputs, the job-summary metrics, the annotations,
        # and the decision to fail the job.
        set -euo pipefail
        emit_metric() {
          if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
        }
        field() {
          printf '%s\n' "$WHITAKER_RESOLUTION" |
            awk -v key="$1" -F= '$1 == key { sub(/^[^=]*=/, ""); print; exit }'
        }
        publish_error() {
          case "$(field error-kind)" in
            digest-conflict) emit_metric "whitaker-installer.digest=conflict" ;;
            unpinned-digest) emit_metric "whitaker-installer.digest=unpinned" ;;
            manifest-unreadable) emit_metric "whitaker-installer.digest=unreadable" ;;
            version-marker-unreadable) emit_metric "whitaker-installer.cache-entry=unreadable" ;;
          esac
          echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::$(field error-message)" >&2
          emit_metric "whitaker-installer.failure=install"
          exit 1
        }
        if [[ -z "${WHITAKER_RESOLUTION//[[:space:]]/}" ]]; then
          echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::resolution produced no record" >&2
          emit_metric "whitaker-installer.failure=install"
          exit 1
        fi
        stale_version="$(field stale-version)"
        if [[ -n "$stale_version" ]]; then
          echo "::notice title=Whitaker installer::path=stale-cache cached-version=${stale_version} version=${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}"
          emit_metric "whitaker-installer.cache-entry=stale"
        fi
        case "$(field status)" in
          cached)
            echo "::notice title=Whitaker installer::path=cache version=${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}"
            emit_metric "whitaker-installer.path=cache"
            printf 'needs-install=false\n' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            ;;
          install)
            {
              printf 'needs-install=true\n'
              printf 'asset=%s\n' "$(field asset)"
              printf 'extension=%s\n' "$(field extension)"
              printf 'installer-name=%s\n' "$(field installer-name)"
              printf 'expected-sha=%s\n' "$(field expected-sha)"
              printf 'trust-anchor=%s\n' "$(field trust-anchor)"
              printf 'staging-dir=%s\n' "$(field staging-dir)"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            ;;
          error) publish_error ;;
          *)
            echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::unreadable resolution record" >&2
            emit_metric "whitaker-installer.failure=install"
            exit 1
            ;;
        esac

    - name: Download Whitaker release
      shell: bash
      env:
        WHITAKER_ASSET: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.asset }}
        WHITAKER_NEEDS_INSTALL: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.needs-install }}
        WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.staging-dir }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version }}
      run: |
        set -Eeuo pipefail
        emit_metric() {
          if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
        }
        trap 'status=$?; echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::exit-code=${status} version=${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}" >&2; emit_metric "whitaker-installer.failure=install"; exit "${status}"' ERR
        if [[ "$WHITAKER_NEEDS_INSTALL" != true ]]; then
          exit 0
        fi
        release_url="https://github.com/leynos/whitaker/releases/download/v${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}"
        rm -rf -- "$WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR"
        mkdir -p -- "$WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR"
        # curl reports the transfer itself. `num_retries` was added in curl
        # 8.9.0, so ask for it only when the runner's curl is new enough and
        # report the attempt count as unknown otherwise.
        write_out='%{http_code} %{size_download} %{time_total}'
        attempts_reported=false
        curl_version="$(curl --version 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR == 1 { print $2 }')"
        if [[ -n "$curl_version" ]] &&
          [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' 8.9.0 "$curl_version" | sort -V | head -n 1)" == 8.9.0 ]]; then
          write_out="${write_out} %{num_retries}"
          attempts_reported=true
        fi
        fetch() {
          local url="$1" target="$2" label="$3"
          local stats status http_code bytes seconds attempts outcome
          set +e
          stats="$(curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 \
            --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 --retry-all-errors \
            --connect-timeout 20 --max-time 300 \
            --write-out "$write_out" "$url" -o "$target")"
          status=$?
          set -e
          http_code="$(printf '%s' "$stats" | awk '{ print ($1 == "" ? "none" : $1) }')"
          bytes="$(printf '%s' "$stats" | awk '{ print ($2 == "" ? "0" : $2) }')"
          seconds="$(printf '%s' "$stats" | awk '{ print ($3 == "" ? "0" : $3) }')"
          attempts=unknown
          if [[ "$attempts_reported" == true ]]; then
            attempts="$(printf '%s' "$stats" | awk '{ print ($4 == "" ? "0" : $4 + 1) }')"
          fi
          outcome=ok
          if (( status != 0 )); then
            outcome=failed
          fi
          echo "::notice title=Whitaker installer transfer::part=${label} outcome=${outcome} http=${http_code} bytes=${bytes} seconds=${seconds} attempts=${attempts}"
          emit_metric "whitaker-installer.transfer.${label}=${outcome} http=${http_code} bytes=${bytes} seconds=${seconds} attempts=${attempts}"
          return "$status"
        }
        fetch "${release_url}/${WHITAKER_ASSET}" "${WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR}/${WHITAKER_ASSET}" archive
        fetch "${release_url}/${WHITAKER_ASSET}.sha256" "${WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR}/${WHITAKER_ASSET}.sha256" sha256

    - name: Verify Whitaker release
      shell: bash
      env:
        WHITAKER_ASSET: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.asset }}
        WHITAKER_EXPECTED_SHA: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.expected-sha }}
        WHITAKER_NEEDS_INSTALL: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.needs-install }}
        WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.staging-dir }}
        WHITAKER_TRUST_ANCHOR: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.trust-anchor }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        emit_metric() {
          if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
        }
        step_error() {
          echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::$1" >&2
          emit_metric "whitaker-installer.failure=install"
          exit 1
        }
        if [[ "$WHITAKER_NEEDS_INSTALL" != true ]]; then
          exit 0
        fi
        # Hash from standard input, never by file name. GNU coreutils
        # sha256sum escapes its output line when the name contains a backslash
        # or a newline: it prefixes the line with a backslash and escapes the
        # offending characters. Windows paths contain backslashes, so passing
        # the name yielded "\<digest>" and failed a correct archive. Reading
        # the file on stdin keeps the name out of the output entirely, so no
        # escaping can arise to be undone.
        compute_sha256() {
          if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            sha256sum < "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
          else
            shasum -a 256 < "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
          fi
        }
        archive="${WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR}/${WHITAKER_ASSET}"
        actual_sha="$(compute_sha256 "$archive")"
        if [[ "$actual_sha" != "$WHITAKER_EXPECTED_SHA" ]]; then
          emit_metric "whitaker-installer.digest=mismatch"
          step_error "archive digest mismatch for ${WHITAKER_ASSET}: expected ${WHITAKER_EXPECTED_SHA} but computed ${actual_sha}"
        fi
        # The sidecar is produced by the release builder, whose sha256sum saw a
        # plain asset name, so it should not be escaped. Strip a leading
        # backslash anyway: a sidecar written on a host that did escape would
        # otherwise fail this comparison for the same reason the archive did.
        sidecar_sha="$(awk 'NR == 1 { sub(/^\\/, "", $1); print $1 }' "${archive}.sha256")"
        if [[ "$sidecar_sha" != "$actual_sha" ]]; then
          emit_metric "whitaker-installer.digest=sidecar-mismatch"
          step_error "release sidecar digest ${sidecar_sha} disagrees with the verified archive digest ${actual_sha} for ${WHITAKER_ASSET}"
        fi
        echo "::notice title=Whitaker installer digest::asset=${WHITAKER_ASSET} outcome=verified anchor=${WHITAKER_TRUST_ANCHOR}"
        emit_metric "whitaker-installer.digest=verified"
        emit_metric "whitaker-installer.trust-anchor=${WHITAKER_TRUST_ANCHOR}"

    - name: Extract Whitaker installer
      shell: bash
      env:
        WHITAKER_ASSET: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.asset }}
        WHITAKER_EXTENSION: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.extension }}
        WHITAKER_NEEDS_INSTALL: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.needs-install }}
        WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.staging-dir }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version }}
        WHITAKER_ZIP_SCRIPT: ${{ github.action_path }}/scripts/extract-zip.py
      run: |
        set -Eeuo pipefail
        emit_metric() {
          if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
        }
        trap 'status=$?; echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::exit-code=${status} version=${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}" >&2; emit_metric "whitaker-installer.failure=install"; exit "${status}"' ERR
        if [[ "$WHITAKER_NEEDS_INSTALL" != true ]]; then
          exit 0
        fi
        archive="${WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR}/${WHITAKER_ASSET}"
        extract_dir="${WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR}/extract"
        mkdir -p -- "$extract_dir"
        # Both release archives hold one top-level directory, but they are not
        # the same format: a gzip tarball everywhere except Windows, where the
        # asset is a zip. The extractor is therefore chosen by what the archive
        # IS, taken from the resolver's `extension` field, rather than by what
        # `tar` happens to be.
        #
        # Probing `tar --version` for GNU was the previous approach and it was
        # wrong on a GitHub-hosted Windows runner. This step's `shell: bash` is
        # Git Bash, whose PATH puts MSYS2's tar ahead of the Windows system
        # directory, so the probe selected GNU tar and GNU tar cannot read a
        # zip. On the Namespace Windows image `tar` did resolve to bsdtar,
        # which reads both, which is why this only surfaced when a consumer
        # moved its Windows lanes to `windows-latest`. See issue #446.
        #
        # Separate calls rather than an options array throughout: macOS runners
        # ship bash 3.2, where expanding an empty array under `set -u` is an
        # unbound variable error.
        extract_tarball() {
          # --force-local tells GNU tar to read a colon in the archive path as
          # part of the name rather than as rmt's host:path syntax. The staging
          # path is normalized upstream, so this is a second line of defence
          # for any other colon; bsdtar rejects the flag outright, hence the
          # probe is kept here, where it is about a flag rather than about
          # which formats the tool can read. GNU tar detects gzip unaided.
          if tar --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q GNU; then
            tar --force-local -xf "$1" --strip-components=1 -C "$2"
          else
            tar -xf "$1" --strip-components=1 -C "$2"
          fi
        }
        system_bsdtar() {
          # The Windows system tar is bsdtar and reads zip. Name it by path
          # rather than reordering PATH: PATH order is what broke this, and
          # putting the system directory first would shadow the GNU find, sort
          # and friends that later steps and actions expect. cygpath converts
          # the native path to the form this Bash understands.
          local native='C:\Windows\System32\tar.exe' candidate
          candidate="$native"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            candidate="$(cygpath -u "$native" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$native")"
          fi
          if [[ -x "$candidate" ]]; then
            printf '%s' "$candidate"
            return 0
          fi
          return 1
        }
        extract_zip() {
          # Two extractors, and a hard failure rather than a silent empty
          # directory if neither is present. The `unzip` command is
          # deliberately not one of them: it is absent from some Windows
          # runner images, and this action's tests already forbid depending on
          # it, so reaching for it here would trade one unstated environment
          # assumption for another.
          #
          # bsdtar is the Windows system tar and honours --strip-components,
          # so on the platform that actually ships zip assets the behaviour is
          # identical to the tarball arm. Python is the fallback for a runner
          # that somehow has neither, and every GitHub-hosted and Ubicloud
          # image ships it.
          local archive_path="$1" destination="$2" bsdtar
          if bsdtar="$(system_bsdtar)"; then
            "$bsdtar" -xf "$archive_path" --strip-components=1 -C "$destination"
            return 0
          fi
          if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            python3 "${WHITAKER_ZIP_SCRIPT}" "$archive_path" "$destination"
            return 0
          fi
          echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::no zip extractor available: neither the Windows system tar nor python3 is present" >&2
          return 1
        }
        case "$WHITAKER_EXTENSION" in
          zip)
            extract_zip "$archive" "$extract_dir"
            ;;
          tar.gz|tgz|tar.xz|tar.bz2|tar)
            extract_tarball "$archive" "$extract_dir"
            ;;
          *)
            # Fail closed. Falling through to tar is how a zip reached GNU tar
            # in the first place.
            #
            # The metric is emitted here rather than left to the ERR trap: an
            # explicit `exit` does not fire it, so without this the step would
            # annotate the failure and then omit it from the job summary that
            # the other failure paths all report to.
            echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::unsupported archive extension ${WHITAKER_EXTENSION:-<empty>} for asset ${WHITAKER_ASSET}" >&2
            emit_metric "whitaker-installer.failure=install"
            exit 1
            ;;
        esac

    - name: Install Whitaker installer
      id: install-whitaker-installer
      shell: bash
      env:
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_NAME: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.installer-name }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_PATH: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-path }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION_PATH: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version-path }}
        WHITAKER_NEEDS_INSTALL: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.needs-install }}
        WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR: ${{ steps.publish-resolution.outputs.staging-dir }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version }}
      run: |
        set -Eeuo pipefail
        emit_metric() {
          if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
        }
        trap 'status=$?; echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::exit-code=${status} version=${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}" >&2; emit_metric "whitaker-installer.failure=install"; exit "${status}"' ERR
        if [[ "$WHITAKER_NEEDS_INSTALL" != true ]]; then
          exit 0
        fi
        mkdir -p -- "$(dirname -- "$WHITAKER_INSTALLER_PATH")"
        install -m 0755 "${WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR}/extract/${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_NAME}" "$WHITAKER_INSTALLER_PATH"
        printf '%s\n' "$WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION" > "$WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION_PATH"
        rm -rf -- "$WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR"
        echo "::notice title=Whitaker installer::path=official-release version=${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}"
        emit_metric "whitaker-installer.path=official-release"

    - name: Verify the published lint assets
      id: rolling-assets
      if: ${{ inputs.ci-mode == 'true' }}
      shell: bash
      env:
        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.github-token }}
        RUNNER_ARCHITECTURE: ${{ runner.arch }}
        RUNNER_OPERATING_SYSTEM: ${{ runner.os }}
        WHITAKER_VERIFY_SCRIPT: ${{ github.action_path }}/scripts/verify_rolling_assets.py
      run: |
        set -Eeuo pipefail
        emit_metric() {
          if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
        }
        case "${RUNNER_OPERATING_SYSTEM}:${RUNNER_ARCHITECTURE}" in
          Linux:X64) target=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu ;;
          Linux:ARM64) target=aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu ;;
          macOS:X64) target=x86_64-apple-darwin ;;
          macOS:ARM64) target=aarch64-apple-darwin ;;
          Windows:X64) target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc ;;
          *)
            echo "::error title=Whitaker rolling assets::unsupported runner ${RUNNER_OPERATING_SYSTEM}/${RUNNER_ARCHITECTURE}" >&2
            emit_metric "whitaker-installer.rolling-assets=unsupported-runner"
            exit 1
            ;;
        esac
        # Five looks over roughly thirty seconds. A republish takes six or
        # seven, so a run that merely arrived mid-publish waits rather than
        # failing, while a genuine gap still fails closed with the URL.
        if ! toolchain="$(python3 "$WHITAKER_VERIFY_SCRIPT" --target "$target" --attempts 5 --interval 6)"; then
          emit_metric "whitaker-installer.rolling-assets=missing"
          exit 1
        fi
        emit_metric "whitaker-installer.rolling-assets=complete"
        emit_metric "whitaker-installer.suite-toolchain=${toolchain}"
        echo "::notice title=Whitaker rolling assets::target=${target} toolchain=${toolchain}"

    - name: Run Whitaker installer
      shell: bash
      env:
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_PATH: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-path }}
        WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION: ${{ steps.validate-inputs.outputs.installer-version }}
        WHITAKER_CRANELIFT: ${{ inputs.cranelift }}
      run: |
        set -Eeuo pipefail
        emit_metric() {
          if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
        }
        trap 'status=$?; echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::exit-code=${status} version=${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}" >&2; emit_metric "whitaker-installer.failure=execution"; exit "${status}"' ERR
        # The two streams are kept apart, so the notices on each stay where
        # the reader expects them, and both are read afterwards: the installer
        # reports a Dylint tool's source fallback on stderr and the suite's on
        # stdout, and a backstop reading one stream is blind to the other.
        installer_log="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/whitaker-installer-output.log"
        installer_err="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/whitaker-installer-errors.log"
        : > "$installer_log"
        : > "$installer_err"
        if [[ ! -x "$WHITAKER_INSTALLER_PATH" ]]; then
          echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::installer was not created at ${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_PATH}" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        # The installer extracts cargo-dylint and dylint-link into its bin
        # directory and then proves each by running it: `cargo dylint` finds
        # its subcommand only on PATH. That directory is on PATH on the Linux
        # and macOS images but not on Windows, where every run therefore
        # failed the proof and fell back to compiling cargo-dylint. It is put
        # on PATH here, and for later steps, which run the tools too.
        # The installer resolves the directory from the user profile on
        # Windows, which Git Bash's HOME need not match, and honours
        # XDG_BIN_HOME elsewhere.
        on_windows_bash=false
        if [[ "${RUNNER_OS:-}" == Windows && -n "${USERPROFILE:-}" ]] &&
          command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          on_windows_bash=true
        fi
        if [[ "$on_windows_bash" == true ]]; then
          tool_bin="$(cygpath -u "$USERPROFILE")/.local/bin"
        else
          tool_bin="${XDG_BIN_HOME:-${HOME}/.local/bin}"
        fi
        export PATH="${tool_bin}:${PATH}"
        if [[ -n "${GITHUB_PATH:-}" && "$on_windows_bash" == true ]]; then
          cygpath -w "$tool_bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        elif [[ -n "${GITHUB_PATH:-}" ]]; then
          printf '%s\n' "$tool_bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        fi
        # The lint suite always comes from the rolling release, and the
        # installer is told to fail rather than build anything from source
        # when a published lint library or Dylint tool archive is missing.
        # Passed unconditionally: validation has already refused an installer
        # older than 0.2.9, the first release that understands the flag.
        # Two calls rather than one with an options array: macOS runners ship
        # bash 3.2, where expanding an empty array under `set -u` is an
        # unbound-variable error.
        emit_metric "whitaker-installer.suite=default-branch-tip"
        # `||` holds back errexit and the ERR trap until stderr has been
        # replayed; `pipefail` makes the status the installer's, not tee's.
        installer_status=0
        if [[ "$WHITAKER_CRANELIFT" == "true" ]]; then
          "$WHITAKER_INSTALLER_PATH" --no-source-fallback --cranelift 2> "$installer_err" | tee "$installer_log" || installer_status=$?
        else
          "$WHITAKER_INSTALLER_PATH" --no-source-fallback 2> "$installer_err" | tee "$installer_log" || installer_status=$?
        fi
        cat "$installer_err" >&2
        # Reported here rather than through the ERR trap: bash 3.2 on the
        # macOS runners does not run the trap for a failing subshell, so the
        # report is written out once, in the trap's own words.
        if (( installer_status != 0 )); then
          echo "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::exit-code=${installer_status} version=${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}" >&2
          emit_metric "whitaker-installer.failure=execution"
          exit "$installer_status"
        fi
        # Read from the installer's own output rather than inferred from a
        # green exit. With the flag in force a source build cannot happen, so
        # this is the backstop that catches an installer that ignored it: its
        # fallback notice is the evidence, and a run that reports one fails.
        suite_source=prebuilt
        if grep -Eqi "falling back|from source with cargo install|installing .* from source" "$installer_log" "$installer_err"; then
          suite_source=source
        fi
        emit_metric "whitaker-installer.suite-source=${suite_source}"
        if [[ "$suite_source" == "source" ]]; then
          echo "::error title=Whitaker installer::the installer built from source instead of using the published binaries; CI must consume them. Re-run once the rolling release is complete" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "::notice title=Whitaker installer::status=complete version=${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION} suite=default-branch-tip suite-source=${suite_source}"
        emit_metric "whitaker-installer.result=success"

scripts/resolve-release.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pure release resolution for the install-whitaker action.
#
# Reads the runner pair, the pinned digest manifest, the caller's requested
# version and optional digest, and the state of any cached installer, then
# prints the resolved contract as `key=value` lines on stdout.
#
# This file performs no externally visible effect. It writes no file, emits no
# job-summary metric, prints no workflow annotation, and reports an expected
# resolution failure as a printed record rather than by exiting non-zero. The
# action's adapter step captures this output and publishes it. Keeping the two
# apart lets the tests exercise the query directly.
#
# `errexit` is deliberately absent: a resolution failure is a result, not a
# crash, and the adapter step owns the ERR trap for genuine internal failures.
set -uo pipefail

# Print "<target> <extension> <installer-name>" for a supported runner pair,
# and nothing for an unsupported one. An unsupported pair is an expected
# result, so this must not return non-zero: the caller's `errtrace` would
# otherwise run its ERR trap inside the command substitution.
resolve_target() {
  case "${RUNNER_OPERATING_SYSTEM}:${RUNNER_ARCHITECTURE}" in
    Linux:X64) echo 'x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu tgz whitaker-installer' ;;
    Linux:ARM64) echo 'aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu tgz whitaker-installer' ;;
    macOS:X64) echo 'x86_64-apple-darwin tgz whitaker-installer' ;;
    macOS:ARM64) echo 'aarch64-apple-darwin tgz whitaker-installer' ;;
    Windows:X64) echo 'x86_64-pc-windows-msvc zip whitaker-installer.exe' ;;
    *) ;;
  esac
}

# Print the digest pinned for an asset, or nothing when it is not pinned.
#
# An absent manifest means nothing is pinned, which is a result. A manifest
# that exists but cannot be read is a failure, and must stay one: degrading it
# to "not pinned" would silently fall back to the caller's digest, or report an
# unpinned asset, when the trust anchor was merely unreadable.
pinned_digest() {
  local manifest="${WHITAKER_DIGEST_MANIFEST:-}"
  if [[ ! -f "$manifest" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ ! -r "$manifest" ]]; then
    return 2
  fi
  awk -v asset="$1" '$2 == asset { print $1; exit }' "$manifest" || return 2
}

# Print the version recorded beside a cached installer, or nothing.
#
# As above, an absent marker is a result and an unreadable one is a failure.
cached_installer_version() {
  local marker="${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION_PATH:-}"
  if [[ ! -f "$marker" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ ! -r "$marker" ]]; then
    return 2
  fi
  awk 'NR == 1 { print $1; exit }' "$marker" || return 2
}

# Print the trust anchor for an asset as "<digest> <source>", or an error
# record when the manifest and the supplied digest cannot agree on one.
resolve_trust_anchor() {
  local asset="$1" pinned_sha supplied_sha
  if ! pinned_sha="$(pinned_digest "$asset")"; then
    printf 'status=error\nerror-kind=manifest-unreadable\nerror-message=%s\n' \
      "could not read the pinned digest manifest at ${WHITAKER_DIGEST_MANIFEST}"
    return 1
  fi
  supplied_sha="${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_SHA256:-}"
  if [[ -n "$pinned_sha" ]]; then
    if [[ -n "$supplied_sha" && "$supplied_sha" != "$pinned_sha" ]]; then
      printf 'status=error\nerror-kind=digest-conflict\nerror-message=%s\n' \
        "installer-sha256 ${supplied_sha} conflicts with the digest pinned for ${asset} (${pinned_sha}); remove the input or correct it"
      return 1
    fi
    printf '%s pinned\n' "$pinned_sha"
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ -n "$supplied_sha" ]]; then
    printf '%s input\n' "$supplied_sha"
    return 0
  fi
  printf 'status=error\nerror-kind=unpinned-digest\nerror-message=%s\n' \
    "no pinned SHA-256 for ${asset}; supply the installer-sha256 input to install version ${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}"
  return 1
}

# Print the whole resolved contract.
resolve_release() {
  local target extension installer_name target_spec
  local asset anchor expected_sha trust_anchor cached_version
  # The runner must be supported before anything else is considered. Reusing a
  # cached installer on an unsupported runner would report success for a
  # platform this action cannot install, and would hide the misconfiguration
  # for as long as the cache survives.
  target_spec="$(resolve_target)"
  if [[ -z "$target_spec" ]]; then
    printf 'status=error\nerror-kind=unsupported-runner\nerror-message=%s\n' \
      "unsupported runner ${RUNNER_OPERATING_SYSTEM}/${RUNNER_ARCHITECTURE}"
    return 0
  fi
  read -r target extension installer_name <<< "$target_spec"
  if [[ -x "$WHITAKER_INSTALLER_PATH" ]]; then
    if ! cached_version="$(cached_installer_version)"; then
      printf 'status=error\nerror-kind=version-marker-unreadable\nerror-message=%s\n' \
        "could not read the installed-version marker at ${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION_PATH}"
      return 0
    fi
    if [[ "$cached_version" == "$WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION" ]]; then
      printf 'status=cached\n'
      return 0
    fi
    printf 'stale-version=%s\n' "${cached_version:-unknown}"
  fi
  asset="whitaker-installer-${target}-v${WHITAKER_INSTALLER_VERSION}.${extension}"
  if ! anchor="$(resolve_trust_anchor "$asset")"; then
    printf '%s\n' "$anchor"
    return 0
  fi
  read -r expected_sha trust_anchor <<< "$anchor"
  printf 'status=install\n'
  printf 'asset=%s\n' "$asset"
  printf 'extension=%s\n' "$extension"
  printf 'installer-name=%s\n' "$installer_name"
  printf 'expected-sha=%s\n' "$expected_sha"
  printf 'trust-anchor=%s\n' "$trust_anchor"
  printf 'staging-dir=%s\n' "$WHITAKER_STAGING_DIR"
}

# Run only when executed, so a test may source the file for one helper.
if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "$0" ]]; then
  resolve_release
fi
scripts/extract-zip.py:
"""Unpack a zip archive, stripping its single top-level directory.

Last-resort arm of the action's zip extraction. The Windows system `tar.exe`
is bsdtar, reads zip and honours ``--strip-components``, so it is tried first
and handles the platform that actually ships zip assets. It does not exist off
Windows, though, and the action must not depend on `unzip`, which some Windows
runner images lack. Every GitHub-hosted and Ubicloud image ships Python 3, so
this keeps the zip path working on a runner that offers neither.

The behaviour matches `tar -xf <archive> --strip-components=1 -C <destination>`
for the shape the Whitaker release actually has: one top-level directory
holding the installer executable. A member outside that directory, or a member
whose path escapes the destination, is refused rather than written, because a
release archive is fetched over the network and this runs before anything has
inspected what it contains.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import sys
import zipfile

STRIP_COMPONENTS = 1


def _reject_unsafe_name(name: str) -> pathlib.PurePosixPath:
    """Parse a member name, refusing one that is absolute or parent-relative.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name
        The member's archive path, which zip always spells with forward
        slashes regardless of the platform that wrote it.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.PurePosixPath
        The parsed member path.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the name is absolute or begins with a parent reference.
    """
    pure = pathlib.PurePosixPath(name)
    leads_upward = bool(pure.parts) and pure.parts[0] == ".."
    if pure.is_absolute() or leads_upward:
        message = f"refusing to extract absolute or parent-relative member {name!r}"
        raise ValueError(message)
    return pure


def _resolve_within(
    target: pathlib.Path,
    destination: pathlib.Path,
    name: str,
) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Resolve a member's output path, refusing one outside ``destination``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target
        The unresolved output path.
    destination
        Directory the archive is being unpacked into.
    name
        The member's archive path, for the error message.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The resolved output path.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the resolved path lies outside ``destination``.
    """
    resolved = target.resolve()
    root = destination.resolve()
    if resolved != root and root not in resolved.parents:
        message = f"refusing to extract {name!r} outside the destination"
        raise ValueError(message)
    return resolved


def stripped_target(
    name: str,
    destination: pathlib.Path,
) -> pathlib.Path | None:
    """Return where a zip member lands once its leading component is stripped.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name
        The member's archive path.
    destination
        Directory the archive is being unpacked into.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path or None
        The resolved output path, or ``None`` when the member has nothing left
        after stripping and so contributes no file.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the member is absolute, or if its stripped path escapes
        ``destination``. Both indicate an archive that is not the one this
        action expects, so extraction stops rather than writing outside the
        staging directory.
    """
    pure = _reject_unsafe_name(name)
    parts = pure.parts[STRIP_COMPONENTS:]
    if not parts:
        return None
    return _resolve_within(destination.joinpath(*parts), destination, name)


def extract(archive: pathlib.Path, destination: pathlib.Path) -> int:
    """Unpack ``archive`` into ``destination``, stripping one path component.

    Parameters
    ----------
    archive
        Path to the zip file.
    destination
        Directory to unpack into. It must already exist.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        The number of files written.
    """
    written = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as package:
        for info in package.infolist():
            if info.is_dir():
                continue
            target = stripped_target(info.filename, destination)
            if target is None:
                continue
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes(package.read(info))
            # The installer must be executable. zip carries Unix permissions
            # only when the writer chose to record them, so they are set here
            # rather than read back out of the archive.
            target.chmod(0o755)
            written += 1
    return written


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    """Run the extractor from the command line.

    Parameters
    ----------
    argv
        The arguments after the program name: exactly two, the path to the
        zip archive and the path to an existing destination directory. The
        action's Bash arm passes both as absolute paths.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        The process exit status.

        ``0``
            Extraction succeeded and wrote at least one file.
        ``1``
            Extraction failed. The archive was unreadable or not a zip, a
            member would have escaped the destination, or the archive held no
            files below its top-level directory. An archive that yields
            nothing is an error rather than a silent success, because exiting
            zero would leave the install step reporting a missing executable
            instead of a bad archive.
        ``2``
            The wrong number of arguments, which is a caller error rather
            than an extraction failure and is distinguished so the two do not
            look alike in a job log.

    Notes
    -----
    Every failure is reported as a GitHub Actions error annotation on standard
    error rather than as a traceback, so the job log names the cause.
    """
    if len(argv) != 2:
        print(
            "usage: extract-zip.py <archive> <destination>",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    archive = pathlib.Path(argv[0])
    destination = pathlib.Path(argv[1])
    try:
        written = extract(archive, destination)
    except (OSError, ValueError, zipfile.BadZipFile) as error:
        print(
            f"::error title=Whitaker installer failed::{error}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1
    if written == 0:
        print(
            "::error title=Whitaker installer failed::the zip asset held no "
            "files below its top-level directory",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
scripts/verify_rolling_assets.py:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Refuse to start an install that would fall back to a source build.

Whitaker republishes its `rolling` release on every merge to `main`. The
publish briefly left the tag without a complete asset set, and a consumer
landed in that gap: chutoro's install began in the same second a republish
deleted the release, could not fetch
`cargo-dylint-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-v6.0.1.tgz`, and quietly built the
Dylint tools from source instead. A source build is slow, unpinned and
invisible, so it looks like a working run.

This check runs before the installer and fails closed when an asset the target
needs is absent, naming the asset and the URL. It retries first, because the
window is short by construction and a run that merely arrived during a
republish should wait rather than fail.

Nothing here trusts a single request: the release's asset list and the
manifest's own contents are both read, so an asset set that is present but
inconsistent with the manifest is caught as well as one that is incomplete.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import typing as typ
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

if typ.TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    import collections.abc as cabc

REPOSITORY = "leynos/whitaker"
ROLLING_TAG = "rolling"
RELEASE_API = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{REPOSITORY}/releases/tags/{ROLLING_TAG}"
DOWNLOAD_BASE = f"https://github.com/{REPOSITORY}/releases/download/{ROLLING_TAG}"

#: Tool archives the installer fetches rather than builds. These are the
#: assets whose absence produced a silent `cargo install`.
DYLINT_TOOL_PREFIXES = ("cargo-dylint-", "dylint-link-")


class AssetsUnavailableError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the rolling release cannot satisfy this target."""


class Attempt(typ.NamedTuple):
    """One bounded retry schedule."""

    count: int
    interval: float


def _read(url: str, token: str | None) -> bytes:
    """Fetch one URL, sending a token when the caller supplied one."""
    request = urllib.request.Request(url)  # noqa: S310 - fixed https origins
    request.add_header("Accept", "application/vnd.github+json")
    if token:
        request.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {token}")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=30) as response:  # noqa: S310
        return typ.cast("bytes", response.read())


def _asset_names(token: str | None) -> set[str]:
    """Return every asset name published on the rolling release."""
    payload = json.loads(_read(RELEASE_API, token))
    return {asset["name"] for asset in payload.get("assets", [])}


def _manifest(target: str, token: str | None) -> dict[str, typ.Any]:
    """Return the per-target manifest the installer will read."""
    url = f"{DOWNLOAD_BASE}/manifest-{target}.json"
    return typ.cast("dict[str, typ.Any]", json.loads(_read(url, token)))


def _missing(target: str, names: set[str], manifest: dict[str, typ.Any]) -> list[str]:
    """Return the assets this target needs and the release does not have.

    The lint archive is derived from the manifest rather than guessed, so a
    manifest that survived a republish while its archive did not is reported
    as missing rather than passing on the manifest's presence alone.
    """
    missing = [
        f"{prefix}{target}-<version>.<tgz|zip>"
        for prefix in DYLINT_TOOL_PREFIXES
        if not any(name.startswith(f"{prefix}{target}-") for name in names)
    ]
    sha = manifest.get("git_sha")
    toolchain = manifest.get("toolchain")
    if not sha or not toolchain:
        message = "manifest is missing git_sha or toolchain"
        raise AssetsUnavailableError(message)
    archive = f"whitaker-lints-{sha}-{toolchain}-{target}.tar.zst"
    if archive not in names:
        missing.append(archive)
    return missing


def verify(target: str, attempts: Attempt, token: str | None) -> str:
    """Return the manifest's toolchain once every needed asset is published.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : str
        The Rust target triple the runner needs.
    attempts : Attempt
        How many times to look, and how long to wait between looks.
    token : str | None
        A GitHub token, used only to avoid the unauthenticated rate limit.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The nightly toolchain the published libraries were built with.

    Raises
    ------
    AssetsUnavailableError
        If the release still cannot satisfy the target after every attempt.
    """
    last: str = "no attempt was made"
    for attempt in range(1, attempts.count + 1):
        try:
            names = _asset_names(token)
            manifest = _manifest(target, token)
        except (urllib.error.URLError, json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as error:
            last = f"could not read the rolling release: {error}"
        else:
            missing = _missing(target, names, manifest)
            if not missing:
                return str(manifest["toolchain"])
            last = "the rolling release is missing: " + ", ".join(missing)
        if attempt < attempts.count:
            # stderr, not stdout. The caller captures this script's stdout as
            # the toolchain, and the retry path is exactly the republish case
            # this loop exists for, so a diagnostic here would end up in the
            # metric every time the retry did its job.
            print(
                f"attempt {attempt}/{attempts.count}: {last}; retrying",
                file=sys.stderr,
                flush=True,
            )
            time.sleep(attempts.interval)
    message = (
        f"{last}. A republish takes a few seconds, so this is either a longer "
        f"outage or a genuine gap in the release. Assets are published under "
        f"{DOWNLOAD_BASE}/."
    )
    raise AssetsUnavailableError(message)


def parse_args(argv: cabc.Sequence[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    """Parse the command line."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--target", required=True, help="Rust target triple")
    parser.add_argument("--attempts", type=int, default=5)
    parser.add_argument("--interval", type=float, default=6.0)
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def main(argv: cabc.Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Verify the rolling assets and print the toolchain, or fail closed."""
    args = parse_args(argv)
    if args.attempts < 1:
        print("::error::attempts must be at least 1", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    token = os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN") or None
    try:
        toolchain = verify(args.target, Attempt(args.attempts, args.interval), token)
    except AssetsUnavailableError as error:
        print(f"::error title=Whitaker rolling assets::{error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(toolchain)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
